name: linear
description: Query and update Linear issues, projects, cycles and teams over GraphQL
long_description: Bring a personal API key from your own Linear workspace; the gateway keeps it off your Sprite and sends it in the Authorization header the way Linear's docs show. Saving, replacing or testing the key runs one small GraphQL query for the key's own user (viewer { id name }) and nothing else. A Sprite can then send any GraphQL query or mutation to Linear's single endpoint, POST /graphql: issues, comments, projects, cycles, teams, labels, documents, initiatives and the rest of the schema. Because Linear's API is one endpoint, the connector cannot narrow it by route; what the key may read or change is set by the key's own Linear permissions (Read, Write, Admin, Create issues, Create comments, and optional team restrictions), so give the key only what the Sprite needs. OAuth, webhooks and file uploads to Linear's storage are not forwarded. Linear's API is free; its rate limit of 2,500 requests and 3,000,000 complexity points per hour per user applies.

examples.title: List the ten most recently updated open issues in a team; replace TEAM_KEY

json.query: query($team: String!) { issues(first: 10, orderBy: updatedAt, filter: { team: { key: { eq: $team } }, state: { type: { nin: ["completed", "canceled"] } } }) { nodes { identifier title priority state { name } assignee { name } url } } }

examples.title: Create an issue (writes to your workspace); replace TEAM_ID

json.query: mutation($input: IssueCreateInput!) { issueCreate(input: $input) { success issue { identifier url } } }

input.title: Hello from a Sprite
input.description: Created through the Sprites Linear connector.

notes: Find team ids with the teams query above. Needs a key with Write or Create issues permission.

examples.title: Add a comment to an issue (writes to your workspace); replace ISSUE_ID

json.query: mutation($input: CommentCreateInput!) { commentCreate(input: $input) { success comment { id url } } }

messages.400: Linear rejected the GraphQL request (%{status}); check the errors array in the body for the query problem
messages.403: This Linear key is not allowed to do that; check the key's permissions and team restrictions
messages.429: Linear rate limit reached (requests or complexity per hour); wait for the Retry-After header and retry
messages.provider_unreachable: Could not reach Linear; retry later

presentation.tagline: Query and update your Linear workspace from a Sprite without putting the API key on it.
presentation.setup: In Linear open Settings → Account → Security & access (linear.app/settings/account/security) and create a personal API key. Pick the smallest permissions the Sprite needs (Read only, or Create issues and Create comments) and restrict it to specific teams if you can; copy the key when it is shown.

notices.title: Billing
notices.body: Linear's API has no per-request charge. Saving or testing the key runs `{ viewer { id name } }`, a one-field query about the key's own user. Linear rate limits each user to 2,500 requests and 3,000,000 complexity points per hour on standard plans (shared across all of that user's keys) and answers 429 with a `Retry-After` header when exceeded.

notices.title: Scope
notices.body: Only `POST /graphql` is forwarded, and it is Linear's whole API: every query and mutation the key is allowed to run, including ones that change issues, projects, teams and, with an Admin key, workspace settings. The connector cannot narrow a GraphQL endpoint by route, so limit the key itself: Linear personal keys can be Read-only, Write, Admin, Create issues or Create comments, and can be restricted to specific teams. OAuth, webhooks and file uploads are not forwarded.

notices.title: Mutations are real
notices.body: Mutations create, update, archive and delete objects in your workspace and notify your teammates like any other change. Prefer a Read-only key unless the Sprite needs to write.

usage_notes: Send `Content-Type: application/json` with a body of `{"query": "...", "variables": {...}}`. GraphQL errors come back in an `errors` array, sometimes with HTTP 200, so check it before trusting `data`.
The schema is browsable at studio.apollographql.com/public/Linear-API/variant/current/home, and the endpoint supports introspection.
Each response carries `X-Complexity` and the `X-RateLimit-*` headers, which the gateway passes back; a single query may cost at most 10,000 complexity points.
